claim: The brain is sensitive to the dose of MeCP2 such that small fluctuations in protein quantity lead to neuropsychiatric disease.
source: The brain is sensitive to the dose of MeCP2 such that small fluctuations in protein quantity lead to neuropsychiatric disease.
evidence: This is a general statement in the abstract that is supported by the subsequent findings and citations in the manuscript.

claim: Eleven individuals with neuropsychiatric disease have copy-number variations spanning NUDT21.
source: In this study, we report eleven individuals with neuropsychiatric disease and copy-number variations spanning NUDT21, which encodes a subunit of pre-mRNA cleavage factor Im.
evidence: The manuscript reports identification of these patients from clinical databases.

claim: NUDT21 encodes a subunit of pre-mRNA cleavage factor Im.
source: In this study, we report eleven individuals with neuropsychiatric disease and copy-number variations spanning NUDT21, which encodes a subunit of pre-mRNA cleavage factor Im.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the function of NUDT21.

claim: NUDT21 regulates MeCP2 protein quantity in patient-derived lymphoblastoid cells.
source: Investigations of MECP2 mRNA and protein abundance in patient-derived lymphoblastoid cells from one NUDT21 deletion and three duplication cases show that NUDT21 regulates MeCP2 protein quantity.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from patient-derived cells shown in the manuscript.

claim: Elevated NUDT21 increases usage of the distal polyadenylation site in the MECP2 3′ UTR.
source: Elevated NUDT21 increases usage of the distal polyadenylation site in the MECP2 3′ UTR, resulting in an enrichment of inefficiently translated long mRNA isoforms.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing changes in mRNA isoform ratios.

claim: Elevated NUDT21 results in an enrichment of inefficiently translated long MECP2 mRNA isoforms.
source: Elevated NUDT21 increases usage of the distal polyadenylation site in the MECP2 3′ UTR, resulting in an enrichment of inefficiently translated long mRNA isoforms.
evidence: This is supported by polyribosome fractionation data showing reduced translation efficiency.

claim: siRNA-mediated knockdown of NUDT21 in duplication patient lymphoblasts restores MeCP2 to normal levels.
source: Furthermore, normalization of NUDT21 via siRNA-mediated knockdown in duplication patient lymphoblasts restores MeCP2 to normal levels.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from siRNA knockdown experiments shown in Figure 2C.

claim: NUDT21 is a novel candidate for intellectual disability and neuropsychiatric disease.
source: Ultimately, we identify NUDT21 as a novel candidate for intellectual disability and neuropsychiatric disease, and elucidate a mechanism of pathogenesis by MeCP2 dysregulation via altered alternative polyadenylation.
evidence: This is inferred from the clinical and molecular data presented in the manuscript.

claim: MeCP2 binds methylated cytosines.
source: Methyl CpG-binding protein 2 (MeCP2) binds methylated cytosines (Lewis et al., 1992, Guo et al., 2014) and affects the expression of thousands of genes (Chahrour et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: MeCP2 affects the expression of thousands of genes.
source: Methyl CpG-binding protein 2 (MeCP2) binds methylated cytosines (Lewis et al., 1992, Guo et al., 2014) and affects the expression of thousands of genes (Chahrour et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Chahrour et al., 2008.

claim: MECP2 loss-of-function is the predominant cause of Rett syndrome.
source: MECP2 loss-of-function is the predominant cause of Rett syndrome, a postnatal neurological disorder that typically manifests around 18 months of age with developmental regression (Amir et al., 1999; Ravn et al., 2005; Pan et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: Rett syndrome is a postnatal neurological disorder that typically manifests around 18 months of age with developmental regression.
source: MECP2 loss-of-function is the predominant cause of Rett syndrome, a postnatal neurological disorder that typically manifests around 18 months of age with developmental regression (Amir et al., 1999; Ravn et al., 2005; Pan et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: MECP2 mutations cause non-specific autism.
source: MECP2 mutations additionally cause other neurological disorders, such as non-specific autism (Carney et al., 2003), Angelman-like syndrome (Imessaoudene et al., 2001), and intellectual disability (Orrico et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Carney et al., 2003.

claim: MECP2 mutations cause Angelman-like syndrome.
source: MECP2 mutations additionally cause other neurological disorders, such as non-specific autism (Carney et al., 2003), Angelman-like syndrome (Imessaoudene et al., 2001), and intellectual disability (Orrico et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Imessaoudene et al., 2001.

claim: MECP2 mutations cause intellectual disability.
source: MECP2 mutations additionally cause other neurological disorders, such as non-specific autism (Carney et al., 2003), Angelman-like syndrome (Imessaoudene et al., 2001), and intellectual disability (Orrico et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Orrico et al., 2000.

claim: Decreased MeCP2 expression has been detected in the brains of patients with autism, Angelman syndrome, and Prader–Willi syndrome in the absence of MECP2 mutations.
source: And in the absence of MECP2 mutations, decreased MeCP2 expression has been detected in the brains of patients with autism, Angelman syndrome, and Prader–Willi syndrome (Samaco et al., 2004; Nagarajan et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Duplications within Xq28 involving MECP2 account for 1% of X-linked intellectual disability.
source: Duplications within Xq28 involving MECP2 account for 1% of X-linked intellectual disability (del Gaudio et al., 2006; Friez et al., 2006; Lugtenberg et al., 2006; Meins et al., 2005; Van Esch et al., 2005; Cox et al., 2003) and triplications encompassing MECP2 lead to a more severe phenotype (del Gaudio et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: Triplications encompassing MECP2 lead to a more severe phenotype than duplications.
source: Duplications within Xq28 involving MECP2 account for 1% of X-linked intellectual disability (del Gaudio et al., 2006; Friez et al., 2006; Lugtenberg et al., 2006; Meins et al., 2005; Van Esch et al., 2005; Cox et al., 2003) and triplications encompassing MECP2 lead to a more severe phenotype (del Gaudio et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citation to del Gaudio et al., 2006.

claim: MECP2 alone within the duplicated and triplicated region is sufficient to cause all the neurological phenotypes of the duplication and triplication syndromes in mice.
source: Mouse studies have established that MECP2 alone within the duplicated and triplicated region is sufficient to cause all the neurological phenotypes of the duplication and triplication syndromes (Collins et al., 2004; Samaco et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to mouse studies.

claim: Small changes in MeCP2 protein level lead to neurocognitive deficits and behavioral abnormalities.
source: Notably, even small changes in MeCP2 protein level lead to neurocognitive deficits and behavioral abnormalities, and the severity of the phenotype correlates with the level of MeCP2 (Chao and Zoghbi, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Chao and Zoghbi, 2012.

claim: The severity of the phenotype correlates with the level of MeCP2.
source: Notably, even small changes in MeCP2 protein level lead to neurocognitive deficits and behavioral abnormalities, and the severity of the phenotype correlates with the level of MeCP2 (Chao and Zoghbi, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Chao and Zoghbi, 2012.

claim: MECP2 has a long 3′ UTR of about 8.5 kb.
source: MECP2 is distinctive for its long 3′ UTR of about 8.5 kb that contains two predominant poly-adenylation (p(A)) sites: a proximal p(A) site located just after the last exon, and a distal p(A) site approximately 8 kb from the final exon, which result in short and long messenger ribonucleic acid (mRNA) isoforms, respectively (Coy et al., 1999; Shahbazian et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: MECP2 contains two predominant polyadenylation sites: a proximal site located just after the last exon, and a distal site approximately 8 kb from the final exon.
source: MECP2 is distinctive for its long 3′ UTR of about 8.5 kb that contains two predominant poly-adenylation (p(A)) sites: a proximal p(A) site located just after the last exon, and a distal p(A) site approximately 8 kb from the final exon, which result in short and long messenger ribonucleic acid (mRNA) isoforms, respectively (Coy et al., 1999; Shahbazian et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The two polyadenylation sites in MECP2 result in short and long mRNA isoforms.
source: MECP2 is distinctive for its long 3′ UTR of about 8.5 kb that contains two predominant poly-adenylation (p(A)) sites: a proximal p(A) site located just after the last exon, and a distal p(A) site approximately 8 kb from the final exon, which result in short and long messenger ribonucleic acid (mRNA) isoforms, respectively (Coy et al., 1999; Shahbazian et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: 3′ UTRs are important for fine-tuning transcript and protein levels because they contain binding sites for regulatory molecules such as RNA-binding proteins and microRNAs.
source: 3′ UTRs are important for fine-tuning transcript and protein levels because they contain binding sites for regulatory molecules such as RNA-binding proteins and microRNAs (miRNAs), (Bartel, 2009, Gennarino et al., 2012; Gennarino et al., 2015) which induce degradation of the mRNA or inhibit its translation.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: RNA-binding proteins and microRNAs induce degradation of mRNA or inhibit its translation.
source: 3′ UTRs are important for fine-tuning transcript and protein levels because they contain binding sites for regulatory molecules such as RNA-binding proteins and microRNAs (miRNAs), (Bartel, 2009, Gennarino et al., 2012; Gennarino et al., 2015) which induce degradation of the mRNA or inhibit its translation.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Long isoforms allow for greater regulation due to an increased number of regulatory elements.
source: Thus, long isoforms allow for greater regulation due to an increased number of regulatory elements.
evidence: This is inferred from the general principle that longer 3' UTRs contain more regulatory binding sites.

claim: The long 3′ UTR of MECP2 harbors more than 50 putative miRNA-binding sites.
source: The long 3′ UTR of MECP2 harbors more than 50 putative miRNA-binding sites, including the miRNAs known to bind MECP2—miR-483-5p, miR-132 and miR-155—and reduce MeCP2 protein abundance (Klein et al., 2007; Kuhn et al., 2010; Han et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: miR-483-5p, miR-132 and miR-155 bind MECP2 and reduce MeCP2 protein abundance.
source: The long 3′ UTR of MECP2 harbors more than 50 putative miRNA-binding sites, including the miRNAs known to bind MECP2—miR-483-5p, miR-132 and miR-155—and reduce MeCP2 protein abundance (Klein et al., 2007; Kuhn et al., 2010; Han et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The proximal polyadenylation site of MECP2 is increasingly used throughout postnatal development, resulting in more short mRNA isoforms and a concomitant increase in protein.
source: The proximal p(A) site of MECP2 is increasingly used throughout postnatal development, resulting in more short mRNA isoforms and a concomitant increase in protein (Balmer et al., 2003), which may be driven by the loss of regulatory binding sites in its 3′ UTR.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Balmer et al., 2003.

claim: The increase in short MECP2 mRNA isoforms during postnatal development may be driven by the loss of regulatory binding sites in its 3′ UTR.
source: The proximal p(A) site of MECP2 is increasingly used throughout postnatal development, resulting in more short mRNA isoforms and a concomitant increase in protein (Balmer et al., 2003), which may be driven by the loss of regulatory binding sites in its 3′ UTR.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on the relationship between 3' UTR length and regulatory elements.

claim: Pre-messenger RNA cleavage factor Im (CFIm) regulates 3′ UTR length by mediating alternative polyadenylation.
source: Pre-messenger RNA cleavage factor Im (CFIm) regulates 3′ UTR length by mediating alternative poly-adenylation (APA) (Millevoi and Vagner, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Millevoi and Vagner, 2010.

claim: CFIm binds pre-messenger mRNA as a heterotetramer that consists of a NUDT21-encoded CFIm25 dimer and any two of the paralogs CFIm59 or CFIm68 (or its splice variant, CFIm72).
source: It binds pre-messenger mRNA as a heterotetramer that consists of a NUDT21-encoded CFIm25 dimer and any two of the paralogs CFIm59 or CFIm68 (or its splice variant, CFIm72) (Kim et al., 2010; Yang et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: In vitro, CFIm25 or CFIm68 knockdown leads to a transcriptome-wide increase in proximal APA site usage.
source: In vitro, CFIm25 or CFIm68 knockdown leads to a transcriptome-wide increase in proximal APA site usage, whereas knockdown of other p(A) proteins, such as CFIm59, CPSF, CSTF, or CFIIm, has minimal effects on APA (Gruber et al., 2012; Masamha et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Knockdown of other polyadenylation proteins, such as CFIm59, CPSF, CSTF, or CFIIm, has minimal effects on APA.
source: In vitro, CFIm25 or CFIm68 knockdown leads to a transcriptome-wide increase in proximal APA site usage, whereas knockdown of other p(A) proteins, such as CFIm59, CPSF, CSTF, or CFIIm, has minimal effects on APA (Gruber et al., 2012; Masamha et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: 59 genes have increased proximal polyadenylation site usage when comparing low- to high-NUDT21 expressing glioblastoma tumors.
source: A total of 59 genes have increased proximal p(A) site usage when comparing low- to high-NUDT21 expressing glioblastoma tumors, and of these, 24 show the same effect as that following CFIm25 knockdown in HeLa cells.
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: Of 59 genes with increased proximal polyadenylation site usage in high-NUDT21 expressing glioblastoma tumors, 24 show the same effect as that following CFIm25 knockdown in HeLa cells.
source: A total of 59 genes have increased proximal p(A) site usage when comparing low- to high-NUDT21 expressing glioblastoma tumors, and of these, 24 show the same effect as that following CFIm25 knockdown in HeLa cells.

claim: MECP2 is the most affected gene by NUDT21 expression changes in glioblastoma tumors.
source: MECP2 is the most affected, and its protein levels increase accordingly (Masamha et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Masamha et al., 2014.

claim: MeCP2 protein levels increase when NUDT21 expression is low in glioblastoma tumors.
source: MECP2 is the most affected, and its protein levels increase accordingly (Masamha et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Masamha et al., 2014.

claim: Clip-seq data show enriched CFIm25 binding of the MECP2 3′ UTR near its polyadenylation sites.
source: Moreover, Clip-seq data show enriched CFIm25 binding of the MECP2 3′ UTR near its p(A) sites (Gruber et al., 2012).

source: As hypothesized, in the duplication patients, we found ∼60% more CFIm25 and ∼50% less MeCP2 protein (Figure 2A), while in the deletion patient, we found ∼50% less CFIm25 and ∼50% more MeCP2 protein (Figure 2B), when compared to 13 age-matched control subjects.
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 2A.

source: As hypothesized, in the duplication patients, we found ∼60% more CFIm25 and ∼50% less MeCP2 protein (Figure 2A), while in the deletion patient, we found ∼50% less CFIm25 and ∼50% more MeCP2 protein (Figure 2B), when compared to 13 age-matched control subjects.

source: We found that NUDT21 knockdown increases MeCP2 in patient-derived lymphoblastoid cells, and that reducing it to wild-type levels in the NUDT21-duplication patients rescues MeCP2 protein levels to that of the healthy controls (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by siRNA knockdown experiments shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Reducing NUDT21 to wild-type levels in NUDT21-duplication patients rescues MeCP2 protein levels to that of healthy controls.

claim: This is the first time that the functional consequence of a candidate gene within a larger CNV has been validated in vitro using patient-derived lymphoblastoid cells.

claim: Duplication patients have increased long MECP2 mRNA isoforms.

claim: Elevated CFIm25 increases distal APA site usage in MECP2.
source: However, using primer pairs that detected only the long 3′ UTR isoform of MECP2, we found that duplication patients have increased long MECP2 (Figure 3A), indicating that elevated CFIm25 increases distal APA site usage.

claim: The deletion patient showed a decrease in the long MECP2 isoform.
source: Conversely, the deletion patient showed a decrease in the long MECP2 isoform, further indicating that NUDT21 levels correlate with MECP2 3′ UTR length (Figure 3A).

claim: NUDT21-duplication patients translate MECP2 less efficiently than healthy controls.
source: We found that the NUDT21-duplication patients translate MECP2 less efficiently than healthy controls, with a ∼50% reduction in total MECP2 mRNA in the polyribosome fraction and a dramatic enrichment of the long isoform in the non-polyribosome fraction (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is supported by polyribosome fractionation data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: NUDT21-duplication patients have approximately 50% reduction in total MECP2 mRNA in the polyribosome fraction.
source: We found that the NUDT21-duplication patients translate MECP2 less efficiently than healthy controls, with a ∼50% reduction in total MECP2 mRNA in the polyribosome fraction and a dramatic enrichment of the long isoform in the non-polyribosome fraction (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is supported by polyribosome fractionation data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: NUDT21-duplication patients have dramatic enrichment of the long MECP2 isoform in the non-polyribosome fraction.

claim: NUDT21-duplication patients have decreased MeCP2 protein despite increased mRNA because NUDT21 promotes distal APA site usage and the elevated RNA pool consists largely of the inefficiently translated long MECP2 isoform.
source: These data support the hypothesis that NUDT21-duplication patients have decreased MeCP2 protein despite increased mRNA because NUDT21 promotes distal APA site usage and the elevated RNA pool consists largely of the inefficiently translated long MECP2 isoform (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a mechanistic interpretation of the data from multiple experiments.

claim: CFIm25 represents the first identified post-transcriptional protein regulator of MeCP2.
source: The CFIm25 subunit of pre-messenger RNA CFIm represents the first identified post-transcriptional protein regulator of MeCP2 and provides important insights into MeCP2 regulation during normal development and disease.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the finding.

claim: No NUDT21-spanning CNVs were found in 30,466 healthy controls.
source: However, we found no NUDT21-spanning CNVs in 30,466 healthy controls (Pinto et al., 2007; Simon-Sanchez et al., 2007; Zogopoulos et al., 2007; International Schizophrenia C, 2008; Jakobsson et al., 2008; Itsara et al., 2009; Kirov et al., 2009; Shaikh et al., 2009; Conrad et al., 2010; International HapMap et al., 2010; Vogler et al., 2010; Banerjee et al., 2011; Campbell et al., 2011; Cooper et al., 2011; Genomes Project et al., 2012), while among our group of 87,200 patients who underwent clinical chromosome microarray analysis, mostly for neurodevelopmental disorders, we identified 11 NUDT21-spanning CNVs (p = 0.025, one-tailed Chi square test without Yates correction), suggesting that CNVs involving NUDT21 are indeed pathogenic.
evidence: This is data from analysis of control databases with multiple citations.

claim: Among 87,200 patients who underwent clinical chromosome microarray analysis, mostly for neurodevelopmental disorders, 11 NUDT21-spanning CNVs were identified.

claim: The clinical presentation of the three individuals with increased NUDT21 copy number and decreased MeCP2 protein levels is not that of classic Rett syndrome.
source: The clinical presentation of the three individuals with increased NUDT21 copy number and decreased MeCP2 protein levels is not that of classic Rett syndrome, which is not surprising since individuals with Rett lack the protein in 50% of their cells, whereas the duplication of NUDT21 causes a partial decrease in all cells.
